analysis: Integration review of all 39 units, mostly documentation plus Swift Autopilot changes. Behavior changes: (1) the Autopilot set widens from the saved selection to every verified cached catalog build, capped at 256 IDs, with no new consent step; (2) coordinator-driven Autopilot downloads (prefetch_model) are default-on with saved consent, with a 50 GiB disk reserve and optional caps; (3) models loaded by an operation are adopted and keep serving after the control lease ends; (4) holds of up to 24h exclude a slot from eviction and idle unload; (5) a transition watchdog cancels stalled operations and preloads; (6) new heartbeat and status fields report busy reasons, adopted/held models and download storage, only with consent; (7) registration now snapshots inventory and selection atomically (CoordinatorClientState.publishModelAutopilot). The visible code fails closed. Download refusals use a closed vocabulary. Disk-free is unknown means refuse. The hash is recomputed locally before the build joins the set. Adoption and holds require consent, set membership, a resident slot and a live weight hash, and they drop when that basis ends. The resume nonce handling is unchanged. The SSD prefix cache (T-041) is untouched. I report one low finding: the default-on, uncapped download surface, a disk-fill/availability concern related to T-016. The threat model has no entry for Autopilot downloads or adoption, so it needs an update. Unverified: ModelDownloader manifest and hash verification on the Autopilot path, the default AutopilotDownloadSettings and the ledger permissions. Also unverified: the definition and strictness of autopilotServesModel against autopilotAllowsModel, whether the new transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) calls in MTPUpgrade (line 127) and ModelLoading (397/434) are balanced on every exit path, the hold_seconds clamp enforcement, and the consumers of registeredAutopilotInventoryIDs. The integration replay was incomplete (318 omitted units), so the next pass should read these sources directly.

findings.detail: The updated docs say that with saved Autopilot consent, a controller can download catalog builds on the operator's behalf unless the operator opts out. Consent was originally given for selecting models, not for bulk downloads. The documented config makes max_storage_gb and max_models default to no cap, so the only default guard is the 50 GiB free-disk reserve. A misbehaving controller or coordinator could use prefetch_model to fill the model-cache volume down to that reserve. That degrades provider availability and widens the A-004 weight-acquisition surface on TB-002. Fix: default to bounded max_storage_gb and max_models, or require a separate explicit download opt-in, and add controller-initiated downloads to the threat model. Enforcing code was not supplied, so the behavior is unverified.
findings.title: Autopilot downloads become default-on for consented Macs with no default storage or model cap
